description:
“When a civilization reaches a certain size and sophistication, monumental things happen.” 

Monumental architecture was used by ancient cultures to express religious devotion, political authority, communal identity, and wealth. Temples, palaces, tombs, city gates, pyramids, amphitheaters, and ceremonial complexes were built on a scale intended to impress both local populations and foreign visitors. Requiring large amounts of labor, materials, and engineering skill, these structures also demonstrated the organizational power of rulers and states while serving as enduring symbols of their civilizations.
